$comment: The M1 crafting chain, per design-bible §5. Every recipe runs as a time-gated industry job (§6). Job durations and level gates are first-draft numbers expected to move once EconSim can measure the economy — which is exactly why they live here rather than in code.

recipes.$comment: The first craft. Deliberately needs no tool, or the chain could never start.

The first recipe no race can satisfy alone. Two of its four raw inputs are always on the far side of the faction line, so building one means either trading at the capital's global market or hauling through contested space -- which is what makes the war economic rather than decorative (ADR-0008). Everything before it stays self-sufficient within a race on purpose, so a new player never stalls waiting for a market that may be empty.

What a composite frame is for. build_alloy_frame had no consumer at all, so the frame -- the one item forcing material across the faction line -- had no standing demand, and EconSim showed cross-faction trade dying inside the first months of a five-year run. Two frames rather than one so the demand is worth a builder's while, and it reuses shuttle sections and thrusters rather than inventing new inputs, so the tier above the shuttle is reachable with skills the player already has. Level 25 leaves shipcrafting somewhere to go past the shuttle's 10 and the frame's 20.
